Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We sketched a draft topology (attached) and flagged a few items the security team wants clarified before we sign the acceptance checklist:

- Control plane authentication model across the peering link (we want mutual mTLS + short-lived certs).
- Egress filtering: can Redwood guarantee no outbound connections from runtime nodes except to allowed KMS endpoints and telemetry sinks?
- KV cache persistence: how are cache artifacts handled on node replacement? Do we have any sensitive key material in caches?

Can your team confirm these items and share a short runbook snippet we can run in our staging cutover? Our timeline is end of next week for the first tenant attach.

I've attached rivermark-vpc-draft.pdf with the annotated topology.

Thanks,
Alex Turner

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I'll attach a short runbook and a control-plane auth excerpt.

- Control plane auth: Redwood supports mutual TLS on the control plane link. For private deployments we recommend a short-lived cert rotation (12h–24h) managed by the customer KMS/HSM; Redwood accepts cert bundles via the private control plane API. We'll send the exact CSR/rotation handshake steps.

- Egress filtering: by default runtime nodes are restricted at the host egress level. We allow explicit allowlists for: customer KMS endpoints, Redwood telemetry, and model artifact registries. We can provide a hardened iptables/ebpf profile you can apply in staging; in your topology we'll also recommend forced egress via the attachment gateway so you get a single choke point for auditing.

- KV cache: the runtime keeps ephemeral KV cache in encrypted memory and an optional encrypted local SSD cache. On node replacement the cache is considered disposable; secrets are not persisted in cleartext. We'll include the cache lifecycle section in the runbook (flush on decommission and rotate session keys).

I've attached a short runbook: redwood-runbook-v1.md and a small network diagram stub for the gateway behaviour. Can Kimberly and Marissa add any ops acceptance checks we should surface to Rivermark?

Next steps: 1) Kimberly to provide the runbook checklist; 2) schedule a 30-min staging validation with Rivermark devops (is Thursday 5/6 09:00 PT ok?).

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — adding a compact acceptance checklist below (we'll paste this into the runbook document):

Acceptance checklist (staging):
- Mutual TLS functional test: exchange test certs, verify mTLS handshake and reject on expired cert.
- Cert rotation: execute rotation script (simulate 24h expiry) and confirm control plane reconnect w/out restart.
- Egress enforcement: apply the egress profile and run outbound connectivity scan from a runtime pod. Confirm only allowed endpoints resolved.
- KV cache lifecycle: create a large session, kill node, confirm no sensitive artifacts persisted; validate flush script output.
- Observability: confirm telemetry events include tenant_id, source_node, and egress decision.
- DR scenario: simulate node replacement and confirm traffic fallback to adjacent tenant gateway.

Minor clarifications for Rivermark:
- We'll need a signed CSR for the initial control plane cert exchange. Your ops team can post it to the private control-plane API endpoint (we'll share the URL in the drive doc).
- For KMS integration, we support AWS KMS and Vault natively; for other HSMs we can accept signed attestations.

Alex — Thursday 5/6 09:00 PT works for our team. Kimberly will lead the runbook walkthrough.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Technical Program Manager, Customer Deployments, Redwood Inference

Kimberly/Sean —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the checklist. A couple of small follow-ups after I reviewed the runbook:

- For cert rotation we prefer a 6–12 hour window (banking ops constraints). Can Redwood support a 6h rotation cadence operationally? If that causes connection churn we can widen, but prefer shorter TTLs.
- On egress: we need to allowlist an internal analytics host that resolves dynamically (analytics.rivermark.internal). Can you propose a DNS-safe pattern for the gateway allowlist?

We'll bring the CSR to the meeting and the devops team will run through the egress scan live. Appreciate Marissa joining for any escalation questions on SLAs. See you Thursday.

—Alex
